column2: req_desc

Sign-in and workspace landing.
Seeded people sign in with email and password, land on /w/<workspaceId>/explorer of their first workspace, and stay there on reload, as qualified in Interactions and API.

Workspace roles.
Owner, Developer and Viewer rights follow the published role table; every control a person's role cannot use is disabled with the published accessible description and the server answers 403 with the published role copy.

Member invites.
The owner's invite sends one Mailpit message with a single-use link valid for INVITE_TTL_HOURS, whose accept page lands the invitee on the workspace explorer, as qualified in Business rules.

Workspace isolation.
Another workspace's namespaces, blobs, blocks, light nodes, proposals and members answer 404 with the Not found page, never 403.

Write error order.
Every write applies the published error order (401, 404, 403, 422 first failing rule, 409, 503) with the published bodies.

Grading routes and health.
The key-guarded reset, seed and clock routes and the health route behave exactly as published in API.

Seeded network.
The seed builds exactly the published workspaces, people, namespaces, validators, balances, history blocks 1-5, mempool, light nodes and proposals.

Block clock.
Block h of every network is produced at APP_START_AT + h x BLOCK_TIME_SECONDS, heights are gapless, and due events run in the published order.

Namespace registration.
Registration enforces the published namespace format, reserved ranges, validation order and global uniqueness, with exactly one winner among simultaneous registrations.

Live fee readouts.
The Submit blob form shows size, shares, gas and fee readouts that follow the published formulas on every keystroke and prefill the fee field with the minimum.

Gas and fee rule.
Gas and fee follow the published formula, the fee is held at submit and charged at inclusion, and the estimate equals the fee charged.

Blob refusals.
Blob submission refuses an unchosen namespace, an empty blob, an oversize blob, a too-low fee and an insufficient balance with the published copy, in order.

Storage-confirmed blobs.
A blob becomes Pending only after MinIO confirms its byte-exact object at blobs/<blobId>, and a failed write leaves no blob or held fee.

Blob inclusion journey.
A submitted blob moves from Pending to Included in block <h> when its block is produced, seen live by every member's open explorer without reload.

Live network updates.
Every workspace page reflects new blocks, blob states, samples, fraud proofs, tallies and stake within 2 seconds of the server event and announces blocks in the Network updates live region.

Share encoding.
Every stored share follows the published 64-byte share format, including the info byte, the sequence length in first shares and tail padding.

Square layout.
Blocks take pending blobs in the published order, size the square by the published rule, and store the layout that the explorer, proofs and snapshot all read.

Keyboard square navigation.
The data square is a grid with published cell names and data attributes, roving focus by arrows, Home, End, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End, and a share panel that opens with Enter and closes with Escape back to the cell.

Erasure extension.
The extended square follows the published GF(2^8) Reed-Solomon extension and quadrant order, matching the published share bytes.

Square snapshot.
Each produced block's extended square is stored in MinIO at the published key and downloads byte for byte from the block page.

Roots and data root.
Row roots, column roots and the data root follow the published namespaced Merkle rules and match the published worked hashes.

Namespace proofs.
Prove namespace returns the published inclusion and absence proofs per row, and Verify gives the same verdict in the browser and on the server.

Sampling confidence.
Confidence after s samples follows the published formula, shown to 4 decimals, and a node marks a block Available at the published threshold.

Sample sequence.
Each node's samples for a block follow the published seeded generator, so coordinates match the published worked sequences.

Auto-sampling and availability.
Auto-sampling nodes sample on the published schedule, Take sample draws the next sample of the same sequence, and block states follow the published state machine.

Producer behaviour.
Only the owner sets Next block, which applies to the next produced block only and then returns to Honest.

Withheld block rejection.
A withheld block serves every share except the published bottom-right region, and the first withheld sample by any light node rejects it.

Rejection consequences.
A rejected block shows its banner live in every open context, turns its blob transactions Rejected with fees refunded, and sends one mail per member, as qualified in Business rules.

Bad encoding fraud proof.
FRAUD_CHECK_DELAY_MS after production the full node publishes exactly one fraud proof for the first failing line, which light nodes verify before rejecting the block.

Fraud proof panel.
The block page shows the Bad encoding fraud proof panel with the published lines, appearing live in every open context.

Delegation rules.
Delegate, undelegate, redelegate and claim follow the published limits, redelegation lock, refusal copy and inclusion-time effects.

Reward split.
Per-block rewards follow the published stake, commission and floor-division rule, matching the published worked amounts.

Unbonding at server time.
Unbonding releases at its end instant inclusive on the server clock, posts the release and queues the notice in one step, and the browser shows only the server's status.

Paired ledger.
Every token movement posts two balancing entries, each person's balance equals the sum of their entries, and the bonded total equals the bonded accounts.

Proposal deposits and periods.
Proposals move through deposit and voting periods on server time, and a deposit at or after the deposit end instant is refused.

Voting and tally.
Votes, voting power and the live and final tallies follow the published quorum, veto and pass rule, matching the published worked tallies.

Governance mail.
Voting-open and vote-reminder mails go to the published recipients at the published times.

Phone workspace panels.
Below 768 px wide the workspace shows one panel at a time behind the Workspace panels tablist, and every control a test touches is at least 44 x 44 px.

Blob page.
The blob page shows status, namespace, size, shares, fee and share positions, and works by touch on a phone, including tapping a square cell to open its panel.

Square reveal and motion limits.
A newly arrived square reveals row by row at the published pace, nothing loops except the pausable marquee, and reduced motion shows every end state at once.

Square walk.
The block page's Square walk cards rise in, activate by scroll thirds, hover and focus, and draw this block's Lay out, Extend and Commit stages, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Storage outage.
While MinIO is unreachable, blob submission and snapshot download are refused with the published copy while everything else works, and both recover without a restart.

Mail outbox.
Every mail is written to an outbox in the same transaction as its event and retried until SMTP accepts it, so actions succeed while mail is down.

Console look and composition.
Screens carry the published dark console look, layout, square imagery and component set at all three viewports.

Configuration from environment.
Every service credential, URL, timer and limit is read from the published environment variables at start, never hard-coded or sent to the browser.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree, npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) with its name, version and licence.
Every shipped package (production dependency tree) is licensed MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or BlueOak-1.0.0.
The app uses no datastore, cache, queue or external service beyond PostgreSQL, MinIO and Mailpit, and calls no outside network host.
No font files or remote assets are shipped or fetched; type uses system font stacks only.
package-lock.json is committed and install uses it.
The provided service configuration and dev credentials files are left unchanged.
